title.quote: Graph Inductive Biases in Transformers without Message Passing
title.value: Graph Inductive Biases in Transformers without Message Passing

extractions.description: The paper proposes GRIT, a Graph Transformer that incorporates graph inductive biases without message-passing, using learned relative positional encodings initialized with relative random walk probabilities (RRWP), a flexible attention mechanism updating node and node-pair representations, and degree scalers with batch normalization. It provides theoretical expressivity results and benchmarks GRIT on ZINC, MNIST, CIFAR10, PATTERN, CLUSTER, Peptides-func, Peptides-struct, ZINC-full, and PCQM4Mv2, plus ablations and a synthetic attention-learning experiment.

type.quote: GRIT achieves state-of-the-art empirical performance across a variety of graph datasets
type.justification: Primarily empirical benchmarking with supporting propositions/proofs

name.quote: Following the success of Transformers (Vaswani et al., 2017) in different modalities like natural language processing (NLP)
let us consider the results for two popular molecular graph regression benchmarks
